identification: Single rough-sawn live-edge slab, roughly 1.5 to 2 m long and about 40 to 50 cm wide, sold as Huon pine. In the photo the timber is quite pale straw to cream, plain grain, fairly wide with bark and a rotted section on neighbours; Huon pine is usually more golden and fine-grained, so species is unconfirmed (could be celery top, or a plain pale Huon sapwood-heavy cut). Gowans sells many near-identical slabs weekly.

viewing_check: Smell and look at the cut end: Huon pine has a strong sweet resinous smell and fine tight growth rings with golden colour. Measure length, width and thickness, check for splits, rot and the bark edge condition. Pale plain slabs of unconfirmed species sit at the bottom of the Gowans range.
